verdicts.rewritten_summary: State Law 4/2023 of 28 February 2023 (BOE no. 51, 1 March 2023), the 'Law for the real and effective equality of trans people and the guarantee of the rights of LGBTI persons' (the 'Trans Law'), applies uniformly across Spain's autonomous communities, including this one: Title II allows adults to rectify their registered sex marker by simple declaration, with no requirement of prior medical diagnosis or treatment, and provides for corresponding document adaptation. The law further mandates public-policy, workplace, health and education measures, and its transitory provisions govern rectification applications pending at entry into force.
verdicts.note: national framework; state law applies uniformly

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch (16 February 2023) reports the Spanish Congress of Deputies' passage of the Trans Law: legal gender recognition by self-identification through a simple administrative process, replacing the previous requirements of a gender-dysphoria diagnosis and two years of medical treatment. The same law expands access to assisted reproduction, strengthens sexuality education, bans medically unnecessary normalising surgery on intersex children before consent, enables parental recognition for unmarried same-sex couples, and prohibits LGBTI discrimination in healthcare, employment and housing; children from age 12 can obtain recognition under conditions, a provision that proved contentious. HRW places the reform within European and international standards against disproportionate requirements for legal gender recognition.
